Prototype Overview

Sahayog — AI-Driven Scheme Matching for Marginalized Entrepreneurs

हर उद्यमी के लिए, सही योजना तक आसान पहुँच

A voice-first, bilingual platform that helps entrepreneurs from marginalized backgrounds — women, rural, disabled, low-income, minority, and tribal — discover the government schemes they actually qualify for, understand why, and get guided help applying.

What this prototype is

A quick summary of the problem and the approach, before you click through the working demo.

The problem

Marginalized entrepreneurs — people who start businesses despite facing social, economic, or institutional disadvantage — often qualify for real government support but never reach it. The barriers aren't ability, they're access: forms that assume literacy and English, no one nearby to explain what's available, and no way to know which of hundreds of schemes actually applies to them.

The approach

Sahayog replaces the form with a conversation. A short AI assessment (by voice or text, in Hindi or English) builds a profile, an explainable matching engine scores and ranks relevant schemes with visible reasoning — not a black-box percentage — and the same guided flow carries the person through documents and application, all the way to a personal dashboard.

The barrier isn't ability. It's access.

Two illustrations from the prototype showing what changes with Sahayog in the loop.

Today, without help

No bank willing to lend, long English-only forms, no one nearby to explain, no road to the nearest office.

With Sahayog

Speak in your language, AI checks every scheme you qualify for, guided help with the hard parts — works over a basic phone.

What's built into this prototype

Prioritized around the Tier 1 must-haves, plus the two Tier 2 "wow" features.

Bilingual + voice

Hindi and English throughout, with voice input and a spoken welcome message.

Conversational AI assessment

Card-based questions instead of a long form, with a live profile-completion meter.

Explainable matching

Every match shows a factor-by-factor breakdown and an AI explanation, not just a percentage.

Document assistant

A per-scheme checklist with plain-language tips on how to get anything missing.

What-If simulator

Shows exactly which missing condition to fix, and how many more schemes it could unlock.

Accessibility mode

Larger text, high contrast, and read-aloud — built in, not an afterthought.

What's next, beyond this prototype

Two things worth planning for, even though they aren't built as working code here.

Reaching people without a smartphone

Not every entrepreneur this platform is meant for owns a smartphone or has reliable data. A real deployment should offer the same core journey over two extra channels: an SMS-based menu (reply with a number to navigate: 1 = describe your business, 2 = check a scheme, 3 = talk to a person), and a toll-free IVR line (a phone call with recorded prompts in Hindi and English, and an option to be connected to a real volunteer). Both would reuse the same scheme database and matching logic already described — only the interface changes.

Full multilingual coverage

The language switcher already shows Bengali, Marathi, Tamil, and Telugu alongside Hindi and English, so the mechanism is ready — but those four are not fully translated yet in this prototype, and it says so honestly rather than silently falling back to English. Getting them production-ready needs a real translation pass (ideally reviewed by a native speaker familiar with government-scheme terminology), not just a mechanical translation of the interface strings.

Sahayog — a prototype for AI-driven scheme matching for marginalized entrepreneurs.
